subject: FinTechCo - follow-up: pricing & regional residency impact
messages:
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.example
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fintechco.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fintechco.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.example, sean.gallagher@redwood.example
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intro / pricing discussion - follow-up & ask

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can model pricing and get Procurement the numbers they need: 

- Traffic profile you shared: baseline ~50M tokens/month, peak up to ~200M tokens/month (bursting for marketing campaigns).
- Residency requirement: EU data residency for EU-origin traffic (you estimated ~60% of tokens from EU customers).
- Target budget you mentioned on the call: rough guide of $1k–$1.5k per 1M tokens.

As next steps for us to build an accurate commercial: can you confirm the following by EOD Monday?
1) Confirm average monthly tokens vs peak month (50M baseline / 200M peak is what I captured).
2) Confirm whether all EU-origin data must be hosted in-region or if pseudonymization/aggregation is acceptable.
3) Any procurement timeline or PO constraints we should know about?

Prelim notes on regional pricing (ballpark): US region: ~$1,000 / 1M tokens; EU region: typically +15–25% premium due to in-region capacity, compliance, and longer audit retention for EU customers. We can provide options to reduce unit costs (caching, prefix/KV caching, model quantization, reserved capacity).

I'll loop in Marissa and Sean on pricing tiers and committed discounts. Attaching a short token report you can paste into procurement if useful (please see attachment).

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: FinTechCo_Monthly_Token_Report.csv (CSV summary of monthly token breakdown)

From: Aisha.Khan@fintechco.com
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.example
Cc: Tom.Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fintechco.com>, FinTechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Intro / pricing discussion - follow-up & ask

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the recap. Confirming details below:

- Avg monthly tokens: 50M (Q1 actuals). Peak month projection: 200M (major campaign months we expect spikes).
- EU residency: yes — any EU-customer data must be stored and processed in EU regions. Pseudonymization is acceptable for some analytics, but core inference and logs need to stay in-region.
- Procurement: looking to get commercial terms in April; hope to sign by end of May. Procurement will want clear $/1M tokens and any surcharges for EU residency documented.

Budget guidance from leadership: target $1,000–$1,500 per 1M tokens depending on commit/term. If you can show two scenarios (self-serve hosted vs reserved/dedicated), that would help.

Attaching the monthly token export we referenced. Procurement will also ask for SOC2 evidence and an architecture note on residency.

Best,
Aisha Khan
Head of Data Products, FinTechCo
--
Attachments: FinTechCo_Monthly_Token_Report.csv (exported from internal usage dashboard)

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.example
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@fintechco.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@fintechco.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.example, sean.gallagher@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intro / pricing discussion - follow-up & ask

Aisha — great, thanks for confirming. Putting some concrete options on the table so Procurement has something to review: 

Option A — Hosted (self-serve)
- US region list price: $1,000 / 1M tokens
- EU region surcharge: +20% => $1,200 / 1M tokens (covers in-region infra, storage, data residency controls)
- No long-term commit required; volume tiers apply (discounts at 100M+/month).

Option B — Reserved / Dedicated (12-month commit)
- US region: $850–$950 / 1M tokens (depending on commit size)
- EU region: add-on ~+15% (our regional reserved infra reduces some overhead vs hosted)
- Committed capacity provides predictable throughput and better unit economics for heavy sustained loads.

Cost levers and unit economics notes:
- KV/prefix caching and request routing can reduce effective tokens billed for repeated prompts by up to 30% (workload dependent).
- Quantization and model selection will impact both latency and tokens-per-inference economics — we can run a short eval on your workload to recommend a model profile.

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal pricing review (Marissa / Sean) — please confirm suggested commit tiers and discount ladders we should propose.
2) I’ll draft a simple commercial (2 scenario lines: pilot 50M/month for 3 months; ramp to 200M/month over 6–9 months) and share for Procurement.
3) Provide SOC2 cert and residency architecture note (we have a template for in-region hosting).

Attaching our updated pricing matrix. Marissa / Sean — any changes to the rates or recommended pilot terms?

Thanks —
Dylan
--
Attachments: Redwood_pricing_matrix_v2.pdf

From: marissa.cole@redwood.example
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.example, sean.gallagher@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: RE: FinTechCo - pricing & residency guidance (internal)

Thanks for the context — internal guidance below for the FinTechCo thread.

Recommended commercial approach:
- Pilot: 50M tokens / month for 3 months at a premium (no commit) so FinTechCo can validate latency and residency. Pilot price: $1,100 / 1M tokens (hosted, EU traffic billed at EU rate).
- Ramp proposal (annual): Offer two tracks:
  * 12-month reserved (recommended for pricing):
    - US: $900 / 1M tokens (commit >= 500M tokens/month)
    - EU: apply regional offset +15% => $1,035 / 1M tokens (we can absorb some via placement on Dedicated in-region for larger commits)
  * Flex/hosted (no commit): US $1,000 / 1M; EU $1,200 / 1M
- Discount ladders: >=1B tokens/month -> additional 20–30% off list depending on term/advance commit.
- EU surcharge & residency: default +15% for EU-hosted inference and longer retention settings; can be reduced if customer takes Dedicated reserved capacity in-region.

Operational asks:
- Provide the SOC2 + residency architecture note (I’ll attach).
- Offer 90-day price protection on the ramp proposal to align with procurement timelines.

Suggested next steps to send to customer:
1) Draft a short commercial summary with Pilot + Ramp options and explicit $/1M tokens by region.
2) Include a one-page residency note and SOC2 link.
3) Offer a 3-month pilot PO and a path to convert to a 12-month reserved contract with the pricing above.

I uploaded a short proposal template (Redwood_proposal_pilot_terms.docx) and updated pricing matrix. Once you share the draft, I’ll add legal/finance-friendly language and the committed discount table.
-Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: Redwood_proposal_pilot_terms.docx; Redwood_pricing_matrix_v2.pdf
